title: Gratin de Pommes de Terre
subtitle: French potato gratin baked in cream and milk
excerpt: Thinly sliced potato baked slowly in a mixture of whole milk and cream with garlic and nutmeg, until the top is deep gold and the inside is soft and set. The definitive gratin dauphinois.
sourceNotes: Gratin dauphinois from the Dauphine region of France; a cornerstone of French domestic cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before, cool, and refrigerate. Reheat covered at 160C for 25 minutes until hot through.

content.text: A proper gratin dauphinois takes time and a low oven. Starchy potatoes work best because they drink in the cream and thicken the liquid as they bake. Do not rinse the slices after cutting.

items.prepNote: peeled and sliced 2mm thin, not rinsed
one halved to rub the dish, one minced
grated, optional for a gratinier top

content.text: Heat the oven to 160C. Rub the inside of the gratin dish with the cut side of a garlic clove, then butter it generously.
Combine the cream, milk, minced garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a saucepan. Warm over a low heat until steaming. Do not boil.
Layer the potato slices in the buttered dish in overlapping rows. Season lightly between layers.
Pour the warm cream mixture over the potato. Press the top layer down gently so the liquid rises around the slices.
Scatter the gruyere on top if using. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 60 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 20 minutes until golden and a knife slides through with no resistance.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving. The gratin firms up as it sits.

items.symptom: The top browns before the potato is cooked.
items.cause: The oven was too hot or the foil was removed too early.
items.fix: Cover with foil again and continue baking. The potato needs time at low heat to soften fully.

items.symptom: The cream has curdled and is grainy.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too high, or the cream was boiled before adding.
items.fix: Make sure the cream is only warmed, not boiled. Bake at no higher than 160C.

items.symptom: The gratin is watery after baking.
items.cause: The potato was rinsed, removing the starch needed to thicken the liquid.
items.fix: Do not rinse potato slices. The starch is what makes the sauce set as it bakes.
